notes.title: Update
notes.content:
[b]What's in this update?[/b]
-Increased Eimear's base level and stats
-Aoife gains Inspired status when a player character dies
-Fixed a bug with Taran's data carrying over in new game plus
-Miscellaneous bug fixes

Eimear is more immediately useful when recruited. She can now carry players through the series of tougher maps after she joins, especially on Story mode. Aoife now gains Inspired (Mov + 2, Hit + 15, and Avo + 10 for 3 turns) when a player character dies. This allows tense moments where a unit's sacrifice motivates Aoife to escape more quickly or survive a tough encounter.

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2094890/Walk_with_the_Living_2/][i]Walk with the Living II[/i] is currently on sale[/url]!

While not ready for a full announcement, my new game is titled [i]Walk with Death[/i], and I've revealed art for two of the game's characters and an enemy in my fancy, new [url=https://discord.gg/eAfunCYBN5]Discord[/url]. The Walk with the Living games also have a home there, so I hope you'll join myself and others for fun chats!

Thanks as always for your support. Don't be a stranger ;)

Yours,
CB

notes.title: Update
notes.content:
[b]What’s in this update?[/b]
-Saving during Battle Prep is now possible
-Enemies in Chapters 7, 8, 9, and 10 have further reduced stats on Story difficulty
-The conditions for Taran’s class are simplified
-Miscellaneous bug fixes

[spoiler]Taran is a secondary character only available in new game plus in order to provide more options on subsequent playthroughs. If any of Aoife’s stats are 6 higher than their base during her recruitment conversation with Taran at the beginning of Chapter 7, Taran’s class will change accordingly. The conditions of his class work on a priority-based system. For the sake of transparency, here’s how Taran’s class changes based on Aoife’s stats, listed in the order of highest priority:
-Aoife’s HP > 25 = Sorcerer
-Aoife’s Mag > 9 = Mage
-Aoife’s Skl > 11 = Archer
-Aoife’s Spd > 13 = Thief
-Aoife’s Lck > 9 = Gryphon Scout
-Aoife’s Def > 7 = Gryphon Knight
-If none of the above conditions are met, Taran’s class will default to Wardsmith[/spoiler]


Two more bits of transparency:

1) [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2094890/Walk_with_the_Living_2/]Walk with the Living 2[/url] could use a lot more love. Currently, the game is looking at having less than 10 reviews a year out from its release. I don't measure the success of Walk with the Living 2 by its commercial success or its number of players. Walk with the Living and its sequel are truly independent games with unique visions, works of art, made with mostly myself in mind as an audience. However, I love that others have enjoyed them, and to make more games and pay the artists I collaborate with, some commercial success is certainly helpful. If you have some time as the year closes, check out Walk with the Living 2, and leave a positive review. It means more than you know.

2) I've begun working on a new game. Expect a full announcement in early 2024 with an anticipated release of mid-2025. The game is another SRPG, this time with a more contemporary setting than the Walk with the Living games. It features a smaller cast and a cabin that will serve as a base to regroup between battles. Here's that cabin:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41552707/2ab53046c160e57671074546dc7c6c6039c29a76.png[/img]

Yours,
CB

notes.title: Update
notes.content:
[b]What's in this update?[/b]
-Clear, concise tutorials now occur on Story difficulty in Chapters 1 and 2 that better teach players the basic mechanics of the game
-New weapon icons for Blaze, Meteor, Gust, Gale, Bolt, Tempest, Radiance, Purify, and Judgment
-Save reminders after battle preparations are now optional based on a choice at the beginning of Chapter 3
-The accuracy formulas of Silence, Stun Baton, and Hexing Rod staves have been drastically simplified to the user’s Mag, Lck, or Res (different for each staff) multiplied by 5; these staves each now have an increased number of uses as well
-The Flame Sword weapon is only earned upon completing the game if the player did not own one previously (if any player currently has a save file with more than one Flame Sword, they’re grandfathered in and will keep however many they have)
-Misc bug fixes

I appreciate those who have played the game since its release and especially those who have left their feedback with a review. If you haven't left a review and you enjoyed the game, consider doing so!

Hope you're doing well and staying safe in the world.

Yours,
CB

notes.title: Update
notes.content:
[b]What's in this this update?[/b]
-Bug fixes (the “Meditate” command can no longer be used with full HP, etc.)
-Presentation improvements (fixed title text not appearing when selecting a destination in the “Explore” menu before chapter 7)
-Adjusted enemy behavior patterns and reinforcements in chapter 6.
-Adjusted enemy placement and behavior in chapter 7.
-Adjusted enemy behavior patterns and reinforcements in chapter 8.

I'm working on allowing the game's controls to be modified from within the game itself; stay tuned for more with that!

If you've enjoyed the game, please leave a review! Non-commercial games receive a lot less attention, so every bit of support is appreciated! It's also nice to hear from folks :)

Relatedly, if you enjoyed the game, have you given it a second playthrough? By my estimation through achievement tracking (which isn't absolute and doesn't include playthroughs before achievements were added), there are still quite a few endings (whole support routes!) that no one has encountered.

This has made me wonder what value the branching paths in games like Walk with the Living provide, especially as I feel currently tangled in smoothing out the more complex webbing of Walk with the Living II. These games are labors of love and deeply personal for me, a fact I hope is obvious. Every character is a reflection of some part of myself. I made Walk with the Living and the sequel with an audience of one in mind: me. My only goals have been to make games that I enjoy playing and tell stories that I love. My most meaningful experiences have been with games that center narrative choice, so that drives my games as well. Agency can be life-altering, even in a virtual space, in a fictional story, especially when agency feels impossible amidst the chaos of daily, real-world living. And yet, I've also found myself lacking the time or desire to play through most games more than once, an experience it seems many who've played Walk with the Living share. I think I like just knowing the variations are there, knowing someone else experienced things differently than I did. In fact, I think a second playthrough often feels like finding Oz behind the curtain. As a storyteller, I think I enjoy the challenges of a branching narrative and the thematic resonances inherent therein. I'm interested to hear from others. What are your thoughts on multiple playthroughs and branching narratives? Regardless, thanks for indulging this little detour ;)

If you haven't done so, check out a couple of the wildly talented artists I worked with on both Walk with the Living and the sequel!
Sprite artist: [url=https://twitter.com/raul_volp]Raul Volpato[/url]
Title art: [url=https://www.instagram.com/ethandavies.jpeg/?hl=en]Ethan Davies[/url]

Please don't hesitate to contact me with your thoughts and feedback!

Until next time,
CB
